facts.fact_text: The applicant intended to organise demonstrations in order to call attention to the situation of those having sustained damage originating in a major bankruptcy case which had attracted considerable media attention in Hungary.
On 5 February 2007 the applicant applied to the Budapest Police Department for acquiescence in a demonstration on 10 March 2007 scheduled in Kossuth Square, in front of Parliament.

On 5 February 2007 the applicant applied to the Budapest Police Department for acquiescence in a demonstration of ongoing nature, from 10 March until 31 October 2007, scheduled in Kossuth Square, in front of Parliament.
On 7 February 2007 the Budapest Police Department refused to deal with the applicant's application for acquiescence in a demonstration on 10 March 2007.
On 7 February 2007 the Budapest Police Department refused to deal with the applicant's application for acquiescence in an ongoing demonstration from 10 March until 31 October 2007.
On 5 March 2007 the National Police Commander upheld the Budapest Police Department's decision of 7 February 2007 refusing to deal with the applicant's applications.

On 23 October 2006 the Budapest Police Department declared the area of Kossuth Square, in front of Parliament, a "security operational zone" (biztonsági műveleti terület) in view of the tumultuous events in Budapest in September 2006.

The Budapest Police Department observed that the "security operational zone" measure remained outside the Budapest Police Department's competence as regards the prohibition of, or acquiescence in, a demonstration.

The Budapest Regional Court pointed out in judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9. that the impugned administrative decisions did not contain any concrete elements establishing the necessity and proportionality of maintaining the "security operational zone" after the prolongation of 22 November 2006.
